newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money slips anew in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money slips anew in quiet market.

text.p: Philippine overnight money slipped to 10.84375 percent from yesterday's 10.875 percent on excess supply and shrinking demand, traders said.
"The market is still very liquid. Nobody wants to lock in their funds in long-term issues. So banks were just lending overnight money," one trader said.
Turnover dwindled to 24.986 billion pesos from 33.473 billion pesos on Wednesday.
"There was no action in the market. Everybody's squarish ... We're just busy wrapping our Christmas gifts," another trader said. Done rates ranged from 10.78125 percent to 11.25 percent.
Despite the liquid market, bankers were still cautious ahead of a possible long New Year weekend.

The Philippines commemmorates the death anniversary of a national hero on Monday, December 30, while January 1 is a national public holiday. Bankers were expecting December 31 to be declared as a public holiday as well, but the presidential palace has not yet made any such announcement.
"We're preparing for an expected tightness during that week due to heavy withdrawals," one trader said. Banks were not too keen on investing in T-bills to preserve their cash position.
Secondary rates were mostly unchanged from yesterday based on a Reuters survey of 10 financial institutions.

Three-month bills were being bid between 10.525 to 11.75 percent, and offered between 11.40 to 11.50 percent. Six-month bills were being bought between 11.80 to 12.0 percent, while being sold 11.65 to 11.80 percent. One-year bills were being bid between 12.15 to 12.40 percent, and offered at 12.05 to 12.15 percent. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
